newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight orders pick up towards end week.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight orders pick up towards end week.

text.p: Fresh inquiry picked up slightly on the sugar freight market on Thursday with the first freight order of raw sugar fixed for Saudi Arabia's refinery at Jeddah, shipbrokers said.

CSR fixed 40,000 tonnes in bulk on subjects from Queensland to Jeddah for December at a rate just above $15, they said. Jean Lion fixed the 1977-built Apostolis II, 15,196 dwt and Maltese flag, to ship 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Syria with Algeria option for prompt dates. New inquiries included Mauritius Sugar Syndicate with an order for 14,250/14,500 tonnes of bulk sugar on its Port Louis to London run for 9/13 December.

Louis Dreyfus was in the market for 4,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Antwerp to Turkey for end November/early December and E D & F Man quoted for a prompt 3,000 tonnes in bags from Continent to Algeria.
Elsewhere, Brazilian port authorities said 186,100 tonnes of sugar, of which 55,500 were bulk, were being loaded at Santos and four ships were waiting to load a further 57,450 tonnes.
In Recife five vessels were loading a total 67,545 tonnes of bagged sugar with one waiting to load another 14,000 tonnes, they said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
